title: Toward Controllable Hierarchical Clock Tree Synthesis with Skew-Latency-Load Tree
problem: Clock tree synthesis must minimize latency and load capacitance while maintaining skew constraints; existing methods make trade-offs between bound skew trees and shallow-light Steiner trees without optimizing both objectives simultaneously.
motivation: Efficient clock tree synthesis is critical infrastructure in chip design, serving as a bridge between placement and routing to enable concurrent optimization of multiple design objectives.
method: SLLT (Skew-Latency-Load Tree) addresses a core challenge in chip design: clock signals need to arrive nearly simultaneously everywhere (tight skew), reach destinations quickly (low latency), and consume minimal power (low load), but traditional methods force you to pick which priority matters most. It solves this by combining skew-focused and speed-efficiency-focused tree construction methods into a unified hierarchical structure that uses partition schemes to divide the design into manageable regions and buffering optimization to strategically place signal amplifiers. The method was validated on chips manufactured at 28nm scale.
key_novelty: SLLT unifies three design goals—skew control (timing uniformity), latency minimization (signal speed), and load optimization (power efficiency)—into a single clock tree instead of requiring a trade-off between them.
contributions: SLLT design combining merits of bound skew trees and Steiner shallow-light trees
Analysis characterizing optimization boundaries and trade-offs between skew and latency-load objectives
Hierarchical CTS framework with integrated partition schemes and buffering optimization
29.45% latency reduction vs OpenROAD and 6.75% vs commercial tools with improved skew, buffer count, and capacitance

metrics.speedup: 29.45% latency reduction vs OpenROAD; 6.75% vs commercial tool
metrics.other: skew constraint maintained, reduced buffer count, reduced clock capacitance

limitations: Validation limited to 28nm process technology; applicability to advanced nodes and other process technologies not discussed.
primary_theme: Clock tree synthesis with unified skew-latency-load optimization
